messages:
Nora (AE): MerchantAtlas wants to replace CompetitorX with Redwood. Primary asks: webhook/function-call parity, prompt->chat mapping, billing reconciliation, security controls for webhooks. Can SE + Ops triage?

Evan (SE): Happy to lead. Short note: CompetitorX exposes a webhook-first flow where model returns 'invoke_webhook' events. Redwood supports function-calling and HTTP webhooks but the schema is different. We'll provide a lightweight adapter.

Mina Ops: POC infra question: they want initial Hosted POC for 2 weeks then Dedicated trial. Need to know if we can rotate keys for the POC and provide ephemeral creds. Also confirm IP allowlist window.

Hiro ML: Prompt parity concern: CompetitorX uses a custom system prompt injected server-side; customers often omit that during migration. We'll include server-prompt capture in the eval harness. Expect a 4-6% behaviour delta unless the system prompt is mirrored.

Leah (Security): Security questionnaire incoming. Key asks: can we sign an addendum for webhook payload retention? They want to know if we support HMAC-signed webhooks and per-customer encryption at rest. If yes, Dedicated/Private may be needed for CMK.

Evan (SE): Example adapter snippet for their engineers to translate CompetitorX events to Redwood function calls: 
```
# pseudo-shim: competitorx webhook -> redwood function call
payload = json.loads(incoming.body)
if payload['type'] == 'invoke_webhook':
    call = {
       'name': payload['webhook_name'],
       'arguments': payload.get('args','')
    }
    call_redwood_function(call)
```
Also note: CompetitorX uses newline-delimited JSON for streaming. Redwood uses SSE; client code needs small change.

Nora (AE): Pricing: they asked how to reconcile token counts between systems and whether Redwood can produce a per-request token report for billing validation during the POC. sales-ops-bot, any guidance?

sales-ops-bot: Hosted product = per-token billing. We can provide per-request token logs for POC audits for up to 14 days. Migration credits handled case-by-case; escalate to RevOps.

Hiro ML: Edge case: CompetitorX silently truncates function arguments larger than 64KB. We should test very large payloads to see if Redwood returns full args (it does) and note the behaviour change. Add this to acceptance cases.

Mina Ops: Draft POC acceptance checklist: 1) webhook/function-call parity tests pass (50 samples) 2) top-1 semantic alignment >= 94% on 150 eval prompts 3) token variance < 7% after tokenization normalization 4) IP allowlist + ephemeral keys verified 5) webhook HMAC verification validated

Leah (Security): Also add: DPA signed, SOC2 report shared, and confirm if EU-only processing needed for specific tenants. I'll send the questionnaire and required artifacts.

Evan (SE): I'll assemble: 1) adapter repo with streaming example and HMAC verification, 2) tokenization diff script, 3) eval harness that captures server-prompt and reranker behavior. Will push by EOD to repo merchantatlas-shim.

Nora (AE): I'll book a joint call with MerchantAtlas tomorrow 9am GMT. Please bring the adapter demo and a short slide on behavioral diffs. :thumbsup:

sales-ops-bot: temporary credentials created for merchantatlas-poc; expire in 14 days.

Mina Ops: CI smoke run queued for merchantatlas-shim branch; will post results here.

Evan (SE): One more note - CompetitorX returns a header 'x-usage-tokens' that rounds up differently. We'll include a reconciliation script to map both usage numbers.

Nora (AE): Awesome. I'll follow up with the invite and the eval set. Thanks team!
